proposal.name: Certified batching of vocabulary heads
proposal.idea: Copy short continuations from the current request, execute their transformer bodies sequentially with the original single-token shapes, and batch only the vocabulary projections. Certify each batched prediction against the reference head’s floating-point behavior. Resolve ambiguity by running the original scalar head on the already computed hidden state. Commit the matching draft prefix and corrective or bonus token, then trim rejected KV entries.
proposal.cost_removed: Amortizes full-vocabulary weight reads across speculative positions. A fully accepted five-position block can replace five 56,623,104-byte head scans with one, removing approximately 226 MB of nominal weight reads before certificate overhead and scalar fallbacks. Transformer arithmetic and traffic remain unchanged for accepted positions; rejected positions waste transformer work. Actual traffic and throughput require measurement.
proposal.source_evidence: candidate/inference.py:24-29 performs a complete target forward and vocabulary argmax for every additional token. Installed mlx-lm 0.32.0 separates model.model from embed_tokens.as_linear, whose implementation is x @ weight.T; KVCache supports offset trimming. Direct checkpoint inspection confirms 30 layers and a tied 49,152-by-576 BF16 head occupying 56,623,104 of 269,030,016 tensor bytes, approximately 21%. Request-local copying has precedent in [LLMA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.04487). [LLM-42](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.17768v2) explains why token agreement alone cannot repair numerically inconsistent KV state.
proposal.generalization: Uses ordinary matrix multiplication, conservative numerical bounds, and request-local speculation without training or target changes. Weight reuse across head queries is hardware-independent. It could matter for large-vocabulary models, including MoE models where the head represents a substantial fraction of active weights. Benefits shrink when the transformer dominates total weight traffic.
proposal.risk: Poor copying acceptance can outweigh all head savings. BF16 ambiguity may require frequent scalar-head fallbacks, and certificate overhead may erase the remaining benefit. Certification must enclose actual scalar and batched accumulation errors, output rounding, and bound-construction errors. Retained transformer state must remain identical to scalar execution; passing current token comparisons alone is insufficient.
proposal.history_relation: Round 0001 failed exact evaluation without a recorded numerical diagnosis. This changes its verifier: all transformer and cache operations retain scalar execution, while numerical uncertainty is confined to the head and resolved locally. Round 0002 passed correctness but achieved 0.771x; this experiment eliminates its quantized screening, shortlist partitioning, and gathered refinement, and amortizes certification across a block. Neither previous round tested this schedule.

research.plan:
1. Implement inside candidate/ only. Preserve reference prefill and first-token selection. Construct a fresh request-local n-gram index from prompt tokens. Retain only immutable weight-derived certificate metadata across requests; perform all drafting and generated-token computation during decode.

2. Retain round 0001’s fixed policy: longest matching suffix up to length 3, most recent observed continuation, at most 4 draft tokens. Index only prompt tokens and committed outputs. Cap draft length k at remaining output slots minus one. Use the original scalar step when no usable draft exists.

3. Maintain the invariant that KV contains committed history except the pending final token. Starting at offset C, process [pending,d1,...,dk] through model.model as k+1 separate calls with shape (1,1). Materialize each normalized hidden state and updated cache before advancing, preserving scalar execution and avoiding retention of unevaluated cache versions. Save the small hidden-state vectors, concatenate them, and invoke the unchanged vocabulary head once.

4. Implement a conservative head certificate. Precompute an outward upper bound M on the largest original head-row L2 norm. For each hidden vector, compute an outward norm bound H. Under verified FP32 accumulation contracts, bound the difference between scalar and batched pre-rounding accumulators by Delta = 2*gamma_(2d)*H*M plus an underflow allowance, where gamma_n = n*u/(1-n*u), u=2^-24, and d=576. Enclose each observed BF16 batch logit’s rounding preimage, expand by Delta, and map through reference BF16 rounding. With a uniform radius across vocabulary rows, only the batch winner and largest competing logit need interval evaluation: certify when the winner’s lower bound strictly exceeds the competitor’s upper bound. Transfer hidden vectors and top-two summaries together once per block and use outward FP64 arithmetic for bounds. Document arithmetic assumptions; unsupported arithmetic, exceptional values, ties, or overlapping intervals require the original scalar head and argmax on the saved (1,1,d) hidden vector. Resolve predictions in order and stop after the first draft mismatch. No empirical margin threshold.

5. If a draft tokens match verified predictions, emit those tokens followed by prediction a. Trim k-a positions, leaving every cache at C+1+a. Preserve fixed-length generation, small budgets, and reference tie behavior. Update the index only with committed tokens.

6. Validate certificates on independent cancellation, tie, rounding-boundary, and exceptional-value cases. Test every acceptance length, cache-capacity crossings, and scalar continuation from retained caches; compare retained KV values as well as tokens. Record acceptance and fallback counts without tuning from benchmark results. Hand unchanged exact evaluation and both performance confirmations to the orchestrator; retain only its required clear improvement.
research.reason: This offers a concrete repair to the unresolved speculative direction while removing substantial head traffic. It preserves scalar transformer computation and provides a local correctness fallback. Acceptance, certificate frequency, and net throughput remain genuine experimental questions.

proposal.name: Certified batching of vocabulary heads
proposal.idea: Copy short continuations from the current request, execute their transformer bodies sequentially using the reference single-token computation, and batch only the vocabulary projections. Certify each prediction against the original scalar head’s floating-point result; resolve ambiguity with that scalar head on the saved native hidden state. Commit the matching prefix and corrective or bonus token, then trim rejected KV positions.
proposal.cost_removed: A fully accepted five-position block can replace five nominal 56,623,104-byte head scans with one, saving 226,492,416 bytes before certificate overhead and scalar fallbacks. This removes head traffic only. Accepted positions retain their transformer work; rejected positions waste transformer work. Actual traffic and throughput require measurement.
proposal.source_evidence: Verified that candidate/inference.py matches reference/inference.py and performs a full forward and argmax per additional token. harness/bench.py starts timing after prefill and synchronization, and shares the model between implementations. The pinned checkpoint has 30 layers, a tied 49,152-by-576 BF16 head, and 269,030,016 total tensor bytes. Installed mlx-lm 0.32.0 separates model.model from embed_tokens.as_linear. KVCache grows in 256-position increments; trimming changes offsets without shrinking allocation. MLX’s source exposes separate scalar and batched dispatch paths, so their arithmetic contracts must be checked independently. [MLX dispatch source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx/v0.32.3/mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp). [LLMA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.04487) supports copying and verification; [LLM-42](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.17768v2) explains why token agreement alone does not establish consistent retained KV.
proposal.generalization: The portable mechanism is reuse of vocabulary weights across speculative head queries through ordinary matrix multiplication. It requires no training, target modification, or cross-request computation reuse. Potential relevance is strongest for large vocabularies and models with a substantial head share of active weights, including some MoE configurations. Benefits diminish for transformer-dominated dense models.
proposal.risk: Low copying acceptance, BF16 rounding ambiguity, synchronization, and fallback can erase the savings. FP32 accumulator storage alone does not establish the proposed error bound. Exactness also requires preserving transformer inputs, execution shapes, and retained cache values and layouts. Offset rollback alone can leave a different allocation after speculative growth.
proposal.history_relation: Round 0001 failed three of five exact-token cases without a numerical diagnosis or performance result. This schedule addresses a plausible failure mode by retaining scalar transformer execution; it is not a demonstrated diagnosis of that failure. Round 0002 passed exact evaluation but achieved approximately 0.771x and 0.781x. This experiment removes its quantized screening, shortlist selection, and gathered refinement. Neither prior round tested this schedule.

review.plan:
1. Implement only inside candidate/. Preserve public interfaces, original prefill computation, and first-token argmax. Return fresh request state containing the ordinary KV cache, prompt history, and an incremental index. Only immutable weight-derived certificate metadata may persist across requests, associated with the correct weight object. Do not modify shared model weights, modules, methods, or global execution settings. Prefill may build the prompt index and weight metadata, but must not draft from the generated first token or compute subsequent tokens.

2. Retain maximum suffix length 3 and maximum draft length 4. When appending committed token H[j], insert H[j-n:j] -> j for each eligible n. This records the most recent occurrence with an observed continuation and excludes an unproductive terminal self-match. Search suffix lengths longest first and copy only already observed tokens, including overlapping spans without extrapolation. Append the supplied first token to history inside decode. Preserve empty output for budgets below one and no decode model call for a one-token budget.

3. Maintain H as prompt plus committed outputs, with pending token H[-1] absent from every layer’s cache. Let C be the common offset, R the remaining output slots, j the selected continuation start, and Q the minimum current capacity across cache key/value arrays. Set k=min(4,R-1,len(H)-j,Q-C-1). If no continuation exists or k<1, use the original scalar model step. This additional capacity cap prevents speculative growth from leaving different cache strides after rejection; scalar steps perform allocation growth exactly as the reference. Require ordinary compatible KVCache objects for this optimized path.

4. Starting at C, process [pending,d1,...,dk] through model.model as k+1 separate calls with the reference token dtype and shape (1,1). Preserve masks, positions, native hidden dtype, and cache layout. Materialize each normalized hidden vector and current cache arrays before advancing; retain only the small native hidden vectors, not old cache versions. Concatenate the hidden vectors without changing their values and call the original vocabulary head once. Preserve each original (1,1,d) hidden array separately for scalar fallback.

5. Establish the numerical contract before enabling certification. Construct an outward bound M >= max_i ||w_i||_2 from original BF16 weights and H >= ||h||_2 for each hidden vector. For scalar and batched pre-conversion accumulators, derive Delta=(gamma_s+gamma_b)*H*M+A_s+A_b, including arithmetic, reduction, underflow, and flush-to-zero errors. The proposed gamma_s=gamma_b=gamma_(2d), d=576, with gamma_n=n*u/(1-n*u) and u=2^-24 is valid only under justified round-to-nearest FP32 arithmetic and the corresponding operation-depth bound. Check actual dispatches for every supported block size, including dot or matrix instructions and any intermediate narrowing. Use a larger analytically justified bound where necessary. FP32 storage, a version check, or empirical agreement is insufficient. Guard input ranges against overflow and unsupported exceptional behavior. Disable this optimized schedule when its static arithmetic contract is unsupported.

6. For each batched logit row, obtain the argmax ID, its value, the largest value at any other vocabulary index, and any required validity flags. Transfer these summaries and losslessly promoted hidden vectors together once per block. For observed batch logit q, enclose the complete rounding preimage of the actual batch output conversion, expand it by Delta, and map its endpoints conservatively through the reference output conversion. Include rounding in norm reductions, square roots, coefficient construction, interval arithmetic, and endpoint conversions; ordinary FP64 calculation followed by one upward adjustment is not sufficient by itself. Under the uniform radius and monotone interval mapping, the largest competing batch logit bounds every competitor. Certify only when the winner’s lower BF16 bound strictly exceeds that competitor’s upper BF16 bound. Ties, exceptional values, unsupported ranges, or overlapping intervals require the original scalar head and argmax on the saved native hidden vector. Resolve positions in order and stop after the first draft mismatch. Fallback must be conditional and must not rerun the transformer.

7. Let a be the consecutive number of drafts satisfying di=p(i-1). Emit d1,...,da followed by pa. Trim k-a positions in place, leaving every cache at C+1+a; do not replace the cache with trim_prompt_cache’s integer return value. Discard rejected hidden states and predictions, and update the index sequentially with committed tokens only. Preserve fixed-length generation after EOS and stop without processing the final pending token. All generated-token indexing, drafting, body execution, head evaluation, certification, transfers, synchronization, fallback, and rollback must occur inside decode.

8. Validate certificate containment against the original scalar head on independent synthetic BF16 inputs, including cancellation, negative scores, zeros, exact ties, BF16 rounding midpoints, exponent boundaries, extreme ranges, and exceptional values. Exercise both certification and forced fallback; numerical agreement tests supplement the error analysis rather than replace it. Test every draft and acceptance length, small budgets, overlapping matches, fallback transitions, and request isolation. On independent real-target cases, compare normalized hidden vectors and every retained KV prefix bitwise against scalar execution, including offsets, shapes, strides, and subsequent scalar continuation. Exercise blocks near capacity boundaries and the scalar growth step. Do not accept token agreement as evidence that divergent KV is harmless.

9. Hand authoritative validation to the orchestrator: unchanged exact-token evaluation, including the complete benchmark workload, followed by both unchanged performance confirmations against the current best. Keep only gains of at least 1.03x in both confirmations. Record accepted lengths, rejected body positions, certification and fallback counts, and throughput without tuning from benchmark results. An unavailable runtime or an unestablished arithmetic contract is an implementation limitation, not a measured experiment result.
review.reason: No fundamental flaw was found in batching only the heads while preserving scalar transformer state. The review repairs cache-allocation rollback and makes certification conditional on justified arithmetic bounds. Correctness and net throughput remain for implementation, evaluation, and benchmarking to establish.

implementation.summary: Implemented request-local copying, scalar transformer execution, batched heads, exact interval certification, conditional scalar fallback, rollback, and counters inside candidate/. Synthetic certificate and mock schedule checks passed. Batching remains disabled because the installed runtime’s arithmetic contract is unestablished. Target validation was unavailable locally because MLX reports no Metal device; authoritative evaluation and benchmarking remain with the orchestrator.
